diagnosis_explanation: Your stomach and the tube leading to it had bleeding. This caused you to have a low red blood cell count. Your heart rhythm was also not steady. You have diabetes. This means your body has trouble using sugar for energy. You also have high blood pressure. Your thyroid gland did not make enough hormones. You have trouble breathing sometimes.
medication_rationale:
Feosol 325 mg daily:
This medicine gives you iron.
It helps your body make new red blood cells.
You may have darker or black stools. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you get stomach pain.
Also call if you get nausea.

Multivitamins one daily:
This medicine gives you vitamins.
It helps your body stay healthy.
You may notice your urine is a brighter yellow. This is normal.
There are usually no side effects to worry about.

Protonix 40 mg twice daily:
This medicine reduces stomach acid.
It helps your stomach heal from bleeding.
You may get headaches. This is common.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.
Also call if your stomach hurts a lot.

KCl 20 mEq daily:
This medicine gives you potassium.
Your body lost potassium with the bleeding.
This helps keep your body working right.
You may get an upset stomach. Take it with food.
Call your doctor if you have heart rhythm changes.

Lasix 40 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra salt and water.
This can lower your blood pressure.
It helps your kidneys work better.
You may need to urinate more often.
Call your doctor if you feel very weak.
Also call if you get leg cramps.
Call right away if you feel dizzy.

Atenolol 50 mg daily:
This medicine helps control your heart rate.
It is used for heart problems and high blood pressure.
You may feel tired. This is common.
Call your doctor if your heart beats too slow.
Also call if you feel short of breath.

Synthroid 80 mcg daily:
This medicine replaces a hormone your thyroid gland makes.
It helps control your body's energy use.
You may feel more energetic. This is good.
Call your doctor if you feel nervous.
Also call if your heart beats too fast.

Actos 30 mg daily:
This medicine helps your body use sugar better.
It is used to treat type 2 diabetes.
You may notice your feet swell a bit.
Call your doctor if you gain weight quickly.
Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Mevacor 40 mg daily:
This medicine helps lower your cholesterol.
High cholesterol can harm your heart.
You may get muscle aches. This is common.
Call your doctor if you get severe muscle pain.
Also call if your skin looks yellow.

Lisinopril 20 mg daily:
This medicine helps relax your blood vessels.
It lowers your blood pressure.
You may get a dry cough. This is common.
Call your doctor if your face or lips swell.
Also call if you feel dizzy.

Coumadin - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine.
It is a blood thinner that was held during your hospital stay.
Your doctor will tell you when to start it again.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and weak after your procedures.
- Take short walks around your home.
- Do not do strenuous activity.
- Eat meals with 1800 calories. Follow the ADA diet.
- Your goal this week is to rest and recover.
- Call your doctor if you have bad stomach pain.
- Call your doctor if you vomit blood.

**Week 2:**
- You might have a little more energy this week.
- You can increase your walking distance slowly.
- Avoid any heavy lifting or hard exercise.
- Continue with your 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.
- Call your doctor if you see blood in your stool.
- Call your doctor if you feel dizzy or faint.

**Week 3:**
- Your body is healing well. You should feel better.
- You can do light chores at home.
- Do not strain during bowel movements.
- Keep following the 1800-calorie ADA diet plan.
- Your goal this week is to walk up and down stairs slowly.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worse stomach pain.
- Call your doctor if your blood sugar is too high or too low.

**Week 4:**
- You should have more energy and feel stronger now.
- You may return to normal light activities.
- Talk to your doctor about returning to work.
- Continue your 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 20 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you have signs of bleeding again.
- Call your doctor if you have a fast heartbeat.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel a steady increase in energy.
- Continue with the 1800-calorie ADA diet.
- Follow your doctor's advice for all follow-up care.
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Severe dizziness or fainting: You could be losing blood.
- Black or tarry stools: This means blood is in your stool.
- Vomiting blood or coffee grounds: This means bleeding in stomach.
- Chest pain or trouble breathing: These could be heart or lung problems.
- Sudden confusion or weakness: This may be a stroke sign.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Bleeding that will not stop with pressure.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Feeling very weak or tired: You may have lost too much blood.
- Fast heart rate or palpitations: This can be a sign of blood loss.
- Throwing up for more than 12 hours: You cannot keep fluids down.
- High fever over 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Stools that are dark but not black: This could be medicine side effects.
- Feeling mild nausea: You can try eating small meals.
- Questions about your Feosol dose: Your doctor can help adjust doses.
- Feeling tired but slowly improving: This can happen after bleeding.
